comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## /rebar-debug RCA — mechanism PROVEN; legitimacy classified NOT-A-BUG (feature-request). No fix applied.

Investigated at origin/main `0b851c8103` in an isolated worktree. Phase 1 completed; the Phase-2
not-a-bug guard held, so **no code change was made** and the disposition is handed to a human.

### Proven mechanism (confirmed by runtime measurement, not by reading source)

A gate op is a multi-phase pipeline; **no component emits anything between command start and the
final verdict at the default log level**. Three contributing facts, all confirmed:

1. **The two longest phases have NO instrumentation at any level.** Measured at
   `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` (rebar's most verbose setting) on `review-plan --force`, total 130.4s:
   - `t+0 -> t+27.1` = **27.1s** silent — material-assembly / store-hydration prologue.
   - `t+52.2 -> t+92.2` = **40.0s** silent — overlap-corpus retrieval
     (`overlap corpus: 852 fresh digests, 3833 skipped`). Pure LOCAL compute, no model call.
2. **The phase logs that do exist are INFO and fire AFTER their phase completes**, never at its
   start: `llm/plan_review/pass1.py:274`, `llm/workflow/container_stage.py:189,235,290`,
   `llm/agent_call.py:381`. The default level is WARNING (`_logging.py:_resolve_level`, :91-100),
   overridable only by `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL` — there is no `--verbose` that raises it.
3. **The sole shared LLM seam emits nothing during the call.** Every gate op funnels through
   `PydanticAIRunner.run` (`llm/runner.py:296`); the leaves are non-streaming
   `agent.run_sync` (`llm/runner.py:540`, `llm/structured_run.py:211`, `:249`). `run_stream` has
   NEVER existed in `src/rebar/llm/` (`git log -S'run_stream'` => zero commits).

### Discriminating experiments (3 runs, same worktree/ticket)

| run | level | LLM | silent prologue | largest later gap | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WARNING (default) | fresh | 54.2s | **85.4s** to verdict | 146.9s |
| 2 | DEBUG | none (reuse path) | 27.2s | — | 27.4s |
| 3 | DEBUG | forced fresh | 27.1s | **40.0s** (overlap retrieval) | 130.4s |

- Run 1 vs Run 3 **rejects** "the signals exist but sit below the default level": raising the level
  reveals per-call lines, yet 27s and 40s holes remain, so those phases have nothing to suppress.
- Run 2 **rejects** "the silence is the model call": it made no model call and was still silent for
  27.2s (11.9s user + 13.0s system of real work).
- Run 1's own verdict reports `llm_ms: 13047` of a **146,900 ms** wall clock — the model is ~9% of
  the run. A streaming-only remedy (the ticket's remedy #2) would therefore NOT break the failure.

Emission plumbing is NOT the gap: run 1's three `enrich_drain` WARNINGs arrived through a pipe
85s before exit, proving `logging`->stderr already flushes promptly mid-run. Nothing chooses to write.

### Legitimacy: `feature-request` — cited, and this is why no fix was applied

Progress emission on gate ops was never built and never removed (not a regression). The
long-silent-run behaviour is, by contrast, **deliberate and recorded twice**:

- **ADR 0089 — "Activity-based liveness under run_sync; async idle-watchdog deferred"** (Accepted
  2026-07-09, ~1 month old, so it states CURRENT intent): LLM gate runs' *"time-to-first-token can
  legitimately be minutes of silence"*; *"No total-runtime timeout anywhere in the gate path"*; the
  reset-on-event stream watchdog *"is NOT built"*, deferred behind a stated trigger (migrating the
  runner to async `agent.run()`), which is unmet. Restated at `docs/config.md:402-406`.
- **`docs/plan-review-gate.md:1415-1424`, section "End-to-end time-to-first-work (honest)"**: the
  review *"takes seconds to minutes depending on ticket size + tier"* and *"no upfront wall-clock
  benchmark is claimed"* — a deliberate refusal, which is what AC-2 of this ticket asks to reverse.

No doc, test, or contract requires a gate op to emit progress or bound its silence. Under the
protocol's three-way test this is "never built, and nothing shows it was designed" =>
**feature-request**, which is fail-closed: a human decides, rather than an agent patching it in.

### Honest counter-argument (why this is not a slam dunk)

ADR 0089's subject is INBOUND liveness — how rebar bounds a hung *model*. It never posed the
outbound question "should rebar announce it is alive?" And its "time-to-first-token" justification
does not reach the two dominant holes, which are **local compute** (27s prologue, 40s overlap
retrieval) with no recorded justification at all. A reviewer could fairly read those two phases as
an unjustified gap rather than an intended design. That is the strongest case for `defect`; it did
not clear the bar of a *cited* authoritative source, so the guard held.

### Recommended disposition (for a human to accept or reject)

1. **Cheapest effective remedy, and ADR 0089 does NOT block it.** The ADR deferred a *stream-event
   idle watchdog* (kills a stalled run; needs async). A *periodic liveness emitter* is a different
   mechanism and is already proven compatible with blocking sync code in this repo:
   `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_heartbeat.py:52-93` runs `threading.Thread(daemon=True)` +
   `stop.wait(interval)`. A ~30s heartbeat to stderr wrapping the gate op would break the failure.
   Natural seams, coarse to fine: `llm/workflow/executor.py:641` (per workflow step),
   `llm/runner.py:296` (per LLM call), `llm/agent_call.py:178,202` (per tool call).
   Constraint: `src/rebar/llm/**` is NOT on the ruff T201 print allowlist (`pyproject.toml:399-440`),
   so it must go through `logging`, not `print`.
2. **Re-scope AC-2.** It asks docs to state an expected duration range, but
   `docs/plan-review-gate.md:1420-1424` deliberately declines to claim a benchmark. The
   defensible doc change is not a benchmark but a **warning that gate ops routinely exceed common
   600s supervisor stall budgets while silent**, plus how to raise them. Note `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S`
   is itself `600` (`llm/config.py:124`) *per request*, and the close path can issue many requests
   (`close_autoresume.py:191` is a `while True` up to `verify.auto_resume_max`), so worst-case
   wall clock is a large multiple of the very budget that killed the reporting agent.
3. If accepted, this should be re-typed from `bug` to a feature/task and given acceptance criteria
   naming a proving command, per the advisory findings its own plan review returned (P1/P9/P10).

No files were changed. Worktree retired.

comments.body:
### Addendum — an EXISTING TEST pins the inverse, and any future fix must not break it

A second independent pass confirmed the three findings above (no `run_stream`/`stream_events`/
`isatty` commit has ever touched `src/rebar/llm/`; ADR 0089 governs; no prior ticket) and found one
citation I had missed that **strengthens** the not-a-bug classification rather than weakening it:

- `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:367` — `test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism`
- `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:181` — `test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout`
- `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:256` — `test_sync_tool_is_not_interrupted_documented_caveat`

These assert that a slow-but-alive run completes and that no total-runtime timer exists — i.e. the
test suite **pins silence-tolerance as correct behaviour**. So the authoritative record does not
merely fail to require progress output; it affirmatively encodes the opposite. That is a hard
constraint on any future implementation: a progress heartbeat must be **purely additive emission**
and must not introduce a total-runtime cap or otherwise truncate a healthy long run, or it will
fail these tests and contradict ADR 0089.

Rejected as authority (checked, not applicable): the `silent`/`silently` language in
`docs/llm-framework.md:336` and `docs/plan-review-gate.md:184,1101` means *semantically* silent
(dropping a finding unrecorded), not output silence; all heartbeat/watchdog machinery in
`docs/concurrency.md:240`, `docs/config.md:312` and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/` belongs to
the reconciler ref-lock lease and the CI bridge canary, a different subsystem that never touches the
LLM gate path; and `tests/unit/workflow/test_executor.py:183-192` ("progress marker") asserts an
in-memory `MemoryRecorder` step status for status polling, not stderr output.

Corroborating field note: open session_log `bane-coach-golly` (`003a-09ae-9983-4007`) records that
running pass1 with `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL=INFO` "made the 'hang' legible" — independently reproducing this
investigation's run-1-vs-run-3 result, and confirming that the only existing mitigation is the
opt-in log level, not a duplicate ticket.

comments.body:
OPERATOR DECISION (2026-09-02): ACCEPT as a small task — but with the SIMPLER "keepalive between operations" design, NOT a background progress-gated heartbeat.

== Approved scope ==
Emit keepalive/liveness output SYNCHRONOUSLY at the natural phase BOUNDARIES of a gate op (between sub-operations), on the main thread, via `logging` to stderr (llm/** is not on the ruff T201 print allowlist). Seams already exist:
  - llm/workflow/executor.py:641  (per workflow step)
  - llm/runner.py:296             (per LLM call)
  - llm/agent_call.py:178,202     (per tool call)
Each emitted line names the phase just completed / about to start + elapsed seconds.

== Explicitly NOT in scope (rejected as over-engineering) ==
  - NO background daemon-thread timer.
  - NO progress-gating / per-phase stall-escalation / health-withdrawal machinery.
  - NO total-runtime cap (stays compatible with ADR 0089 + the silence-tolerance tests
    test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism / test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout).

== Why this is sufficient (and arguably better) ==
  - Progress-linked BY CONSTRUCTION: a line prints only when a phase actually completes, so it
    can never falsely signal liveness during a hang — synchronous emission cannot mask a stall.
  - Breaks the reported failure: measured phases were 27s / 40s / ~85s-to-verdict, so the worst-
    case silent gap becomes the longest SINGLE phase (tens of seconds), never the whole op's
    ~600s silence that killed the reporting agent.

== Residual (accepted, backstopped) ==
  A single phase legitimately exceeding the watchdog budget (e.g. one model call >600s) is still
  silent for that phase. Backstopped by (a) the per-request read timeout httpx.Timeout(cfg.timeout_s)
  default 600s (structured_run.py:419-427, anthropic_model.py:122 "never unbounded"), and
  (b) the re-scoped AC-2 doc warning below.

== AC-2 re-scope ==
Not a duration BENCHMARK (docs deliberately decline one, plan-review-gate.md:1420-1424). Instead:
a WARNING in the gate docs that gate ops routinely exceed common 600s supervisor stall budgets
while silent between phases, and how to raise those budgets. Note DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=600 is
per-request and the close path can issue many (close_autoresume.py while-loop up to
verify.auto_resume_max), so worst-case wall clock is a large multiple of that budget.

== Lifecycle ==
Retype from bug -> task; acceptance criteria name a proving command (a gate invocation on a repo
where the call takes minutes emits >=1 keepalive line well inside a 600s window). Not-a-bug
(feature-request) per prior RCA, now operator-approved to build.

comments.body:
FINALIZED SCOPE (operator-approved 2026-09-02) — supersedes the phase-boundary-only note above.

Keepalive granularity = BETWEEN LLM CALLS (agentic round-trips), coalesced by elapsed time.

WHAT TO EMIT:
- A keepalive line at LLM-call boundaries (the load-bearing case: an agentic phase with N model
  calls + tool use must not go silent for the whole phase; per-call bounds the worst-case silent
  gap to a single model round-trip, already transport-capped at 600s).
- Also at tool-call and phase boundaries, BUT coalesced: only actually emit if >= ~15-30s since the
  last keepalive line. A burst of fast tool calls collapses to nothing; a long call/tool triggers
  a line. This is ONE last-emit-timestamp comparison at the existing seam.
- Content: lightweight only — phase name + call index + elapsed seconds. NO prompt/response payload
  (avoids noise AND avoids leaking sensitive content).
- Via `logging` to stderr, at/above the DEFAULT effective level so it actually resets a supervisor
  stall watchdog (today's phase logs are INFO and sit below the default WARNING level -> useless;
  this must NOT repeat that). llm/** is not on the ruff T201 print allowlist, so `logging`, not print.

SEAMS (from RCA): llm/runner.py:296 (per LLM call, primary), llm/agent_call.py:178,202 (per tool
call), llm/workflow/executor.py:641 (per workflow step).

EXPLICITLY OUT (rejected as over-engineering): no background daemon-thread timer; no progress-gating
/ stall-escalation / health-withdrawal; no total-runtime cap. Emission is synchronous + main-thread,
therefore progress-linked BY CONSTRUCTION and cannot mask a hang.

CADENCE DRIVER: "no silent inter-emission gap approaches the 600s budget," not "emit as often as
possible."

RESIDUAL (accepted, backstopped): a single phase/call legitimately exceeding the budget is silent
for its duration -> backstopped by the per-request read timeout httpx.Timeout(cfg.timeout_s) default
600s (structured_run.py:419-427; anthropic_model.py:122 "never unbounded") + the AC-2 doc warning.

AC-2 (re-scoped): NOT a duration benchmark (docs decline one, plan-review-gate.md:1420-1424).
Instead a doc WARNING that gate ops routinely exceed common 600s supervisor stall budgets while
silent between calls, and how to raise those budgets; note DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=600 is per-request and
the close path can issue many (close_autoresume while-loop up to verify.auto_resume_max).

LIFECYCLE: retype bug -> task. ACs: (1) a gate invocation that takes minutes emits >=1 keepalive
line well inside a 600s window, driven by real per-call progress; (2) bursts of rapid tool calls do
NOT produce a line per call (coalesced); (3) the doc warning lands; (4) silence-tolerance tests
test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism + test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout stay
GREEN (purely additive; no total-runtime cap).

compiled_state.description:
## Operator-approved scope
Implement the finalized 2026-09-02 scope from the ticket comments: rebar LLM gate operations emit lightweight keepalive lines synchronously at existing progress seams so supervising stall watchdogs are not silent for an entire multi-call gate phase.

## Implementation plan
1. Add a small shared LLM keepalive helper with `KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S = 25.0` and a single last-emit-timestamp comparison. It logs at WARNING so the line reaches stderr at rebar's default effective log level (WARNING) without `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL`.
2. Guard the timestamp comparison/update with a simple in-process lock so coalescing is race-free if runner, tool, or workflow emit sites are crossed concurrently.
3. Emit through that helper at the primary per-LLM-call seam in `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, including operation/phase name, call index when available, and elapsed seconds only.
4. Ensure keepalive content excludes prompt text, model responses, tool arguments, and tool payloads.
5. Emit through the same helper inside the per-tool `call_tool` boundary in `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py`: the `_MemoNudgeToolset` and `_SteeringToolset` wrappers built by `_memo_toolsets` / `_steering_toolsets`, which fire per tool call during the agentic loop on the event-loop thread. Do not use post-run helpers such as `log_call_success` for this requirement.
6. Emit through the same helper at workflow-step boundaries in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py`, adjacent to the existing per-step `_t_step` / `_dispatch(...)` timing boundary where workflow steps are actually iterated.
7. Use the shared elapsed-time coalescing so bursts of fast tool/step calls do not produce one line per call.
8. Keep the change purely additive: no background daemon thread, no progress-gating/stall escalation/health withdrawal, no total-runtime cap, and no change to existing timeout behavior, preserving ADR 0089.
9. Keep `KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S` as a fixed module constant rather than config surface because the approved scope explicitly requested no new config unless trivial; supervisor-specific tuning remains the supervisor's no-output budget, documented below.
10. Add a short warning to gate documentation that gate ops can exceed common 600s supervisor stall budgets while silent between calls; the new keepalive mitigates multi-call silence, but a single very long request can still exceed a budget. Note `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=600` is per request and close can make many requests, so supervisors may need larger no-output budgets.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Default-level keepalive: a gate/agentic-loop path crossing per-call progress emits at least one keepalive line to stderr/log capture at the default WARNING level. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py::test_runner_keepalive_reaches_default_warning_level -q`.
- [ ] Coalescing: rapid tool-call/step bursts do not emit one line per call. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py::test_tool_keepalives_are_coalesced -q`.
- [ ] Concurrent coalescing: simultaneous emit attempts crossing the guarded timestamp comparison still coalesce to one keepalive for an interval. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py::test_concurrent_keepalives_share_one_interval -q`.
- [ ] Content safety: keepalive lines include only operation/phase name, call index where available, and elapsed seconds. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py -q`.
- [ ] ADR 0089 compatibility: no timer thread, total-runtime cap, timeout change, or interruption of slow-but-alive calls is introduced. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout -q`.
- [ ] Documentation: the supervisor stall-budget warning lands in the gate/config docs. Verified by review of `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and/or `docs/config.md` plus `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`.

## Testing
Targeted RED/GREEN commands:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout -q`

Review preflight commands:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

Empirical default-level check:
- Run a fast deterministic gate/runner invocation without `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL` and assert the keepalive is written through logging at WARNING, which reaches stderr/log capture under the default effective level.

## Portability
The implementation is pure Python logging plus deterministic unit tests. It does not depend on any CI provider, external daemon, terminal feature, or platform-specific supervisor, satisfying project portability.

file_impact.reason: New shared keepalive coalescing/logging helper for LLM gate progress seams.
Actual per-workflow-step dispatch/timing boundary for keepalive emission.
RED-first deterministic coverage for default-level keepalive emission and coalescing.
Existing silence-tolerance tests must remain green; no planned source changes unless test integration requires import adjustments.
Configuration documentation note that DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S is per request and supervisors may need higher no-output budgets.
